Did you ever try a real amp in the studio on this album? LePage: There was one time we re-amped with an amp, and we were like, “This sounds worse.” It was just whatever random amp that guy had in his studio.

entertainment.title: Two C.I.A. Agents Walk Into a Bar on Rapa Nui: Inside ‘Wild Horse Nine’
entertainment.summary: A tangent-filled conversation with Martin McDonagh, John Malkovich, and Sam Rockwell about conspiracy theories, America, and their new movie
entertainment.body:
“Hey, how come John gets a table?” Sam Rockwell asks, shooting faux-daggers out of his eyes. “Where’s my table?!” “I get a table, Sam, because I’m fucking better than you,” John Malkovich calmly replies, in what can only be described as a John Malkovich voice.

“Just because you’re fucking better than me doesn’t mean you should get a fucking table, man,” Rockwell whines, a pained look on his voice. You wonder if fisticuffs between the two award-winning actors are about to commence. Then, with perfect comic timing, Rockwell turns to the person sitting opposite him and his Wild Horse Nine costar, and pretends that he’s only just noticed the interviewer in the room. “Ohheyhow’sitgoingI’mSam,” he rapidly says, sticking out his hand as Malkovich giggles. “Welcome to the Battle of the Tables.”

Over in the corner, Martin McDonagh is watching the duo bicker like an old married couple. We’re all in a hotel room that’s been given an exotic regional makeover, the sort of movie-themed set designing that will be the background of a million junket interviews and reminds you that we’ve once again entered an awards season in hell. Crew members float in and out, gingerly stepping around boom mics and video equipment. Publicists scurry around, checking phones and murmuring among themselves about who gets lunch when. And amidst all the hullabaloo sits the British writer-director, smiling to himself. The profanity-laden back-and-forth about the injustice of one person getting a chair with a tiny stand next to it sounds like something straight out of his movies. You can practically see him taking mental notes.

Wild Horse Nine is filled with the kind of rants and banter that’s defined McDonagh’s work since his early days as a playwright, with Rockwell and Malkovich as C.I.A. agents waxing poetic about why certain countries have superior cheese, the benefit of putting surreal imagery on homemade bombs, and imagining a Western made from the perspective of a horse. His latest, which is in theaters now, mines a formula that goes as far back as The Lonesome West, the 1997 play that concludes his reputation-making “Lehane Trilogy,” and doubles as an unofficial companion piece to In Bruges, McDonagh’s 2008 debut feature about hitmen wandering around Belgium. Take two guys, give them uproariously funny dialogue that splits the middle between Harold Pinter and David Mamet, add in few dashes of shocking violence, and let everything reach a full boil.

entertainment.title: This Former Physics Teacher Recorded an Album of Folky Songs Inspired by Sonar
entertainment.summary: On Echolocationism , Ben Labat, who once led the alt-rock band the Terms, looks to marine-life navigation for musical ideas: "It’s really about finding that new path"
entertainment.body:
Ben Labat has been on the verge of stardom. He had a major-label deal with Capitol Records, and his music has been featured in zeitgeist television shows from The Real World to Jersey Shore . But after a career that spans nearly three decades, the Louisiana native has found himself most comfortable when he’s processing his own life through writing and singing folk-rock tunes.

Labat says that the more music — aided by artificial intelligence and technology — has moved away from simple approaches to lyrics and melodies, the more he’s been drawn back to them.

“I like the reverse of AI and the use of technology, and all the wild and crazy things you can do with it in film and writing and graphic design and music” Labat tells Rolling Stone . “It felt good to just be me and an acoustic guitar.”

But Labat did find at least some inspiration in science for his new album Echolocationism . A one-time physics teacher, he’s fascinated by the sonar-like senses that marine animals like dolphins use to navigate the open ocean — called “echolocation” (hence the title of his album). Echolocationism is his seventh studio LP since 2006, and he wrote 10 of the 11 tracks himself. Only a cover of Harry Styles’ hit “Matilda,” which Labat says is his daughter’s favorite song, keeps the album from being entirely original material.

He recorded Echolocationism himself, playing a Martin D-28 acoustic guitar that his grandfather once owned. The guitar had been sold for a time, but Labat bought it back and was compelled to build an album around it. “I started digging through the songs that never made it to a full-band cut, and then they just kind of all came together,” he says.

The album opens with “Set a New Course,” which Labat delivers in a gravelly Louisiana drawl over that very acoustic guitar. You can hear echoes of Springsteen’s best stripped-down material in the melody, especially when Labat laments, “Life tuned me up and played me like a song/so I set a new course.” Editor’s picks The 250 Greatest Albums of the 21st Century So Far The 100 Best TV Episodes of All Time The 500 Greatest Albums of All Time 100 Best Movies of the 21st Century

“It’s really about finding that new path,” Labat says. “Whether it’s a job or a relationship, moving to a new city, having children. I’m trying to be a parent and explain that things are not always gonna go your way. You’re gonna have to embrace the change, and sometimes, things are gonna happen and you won’t be the same. The way you look at things and how you react will be different.”

entertainment.title: 5 TV Shows To Watch If You Like Anna Pigeon
entertainment.summary: If you loved the first season of Anna Pigeon, these top notch crime dramas will keep you busy and entertained while the world waits for Season 2.
entertainment.body:
USA Network Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Folks who adored the first season will be happy to know that USA Network has renewed "Anna Pigeon" for Season 2 . After a dry spell of scripted programs, it appears that the cable network is getting back in the game with this outdoorsy crime drama. Tracy Spiridakos plays the titular park ranger, as Season 1 sends Anna out into the wild just in time for things to go wrong at Glacier National Park. But if you've already binged every episode, it may be time to look elsewhere.

While we await "Anna Pigeon" Season 2, there's no reason that you can't pivot to some other (similar) television adventures. Fans who enjoy the National Park/outdoor aesthetic, the neo-Western flair, book-to-screen adaptations (the USA series is based on the crime novels by Nevada Barr), or the simple police procedural style have plenty of options to choose from. Recent years have offered plenty of options on network, cable, or streaming platforms, and each has its own merits.

"Anna Pigeon" may have finished up its first season, but here are some TV dramas that may scratch the same itch. Just be careful where you step, because things can get wild out there.

Paramount+ Perhaps one of the most aesthetically similar shows to "Anna Pigeon" is "Joe Pickett." What began as a Spectrum Original was soon co-opted by Paramount+ as the streamer expanded its collection of neo-Western productions. Based on the mystery novels by author C.J. Box, this two-season crime drama follows the titular Wyoming game warden (played by Michael Dorman) as he patrols the forestlands that border Yellowstone National Park — and yes, this feels far more national park-y than "Yellowstone."

"Joe Pickett" tackles a new mystery each season, as Joe finds himself involved in whatever new conspiracy, murder, or strange occurrence that happens in the wilderness surrounding Twelve Sleep County. Alongside his wife, Marybeth (Julianna Guill), and daughters, Joe wrestles with his own darkness and fights to curb his negative impulses for the sake of his family. A true Western hero with a strong moral code, Joe Pickett is the type of hero worth investing in.

Sadly, "Joe Pickett" was canceled after two seasons , which came as a blow to those of us hoping for more. Given that each season followed a largely serialized mystery, the show doesn't leave too many loose ends, though it does set up some teases that will never be paid off. Fortunately, C.J. Box still drops a new book once a year, so Joe is alive and well on the page.

entertainment.title: Why Are So Many Artists Dropping Holiday Music?
entertainment.summary: Here's your guide to everyone releasing holiday projects, from Olivia Rodrigo to Alanis Morissette to Hilary Duff
entertainment.body:
We get it, we’re only a week into November … but holiday season is just around the corner, and Mariah Carey’s “All I Want For Christmas Is You” is quickly defrosting. This season, it feels like every artist is trying to throw their hat into the holiday music canon. From Olivia Rodrigo to Alanis Morissette and Thalia, there’s so many exciting holiday releases out or still on the horizon. We’ve compiled some of the best holiday music releases in this official guide, just in case you wanted a refresh from the classics, Carey, and Michael Bublé . Check it out below, and if it inspires you to take the Christmas tree out of storage, don’t blame us.

Hilary Duff kicked the holiday season off early this year, releasing her Holiday Things five-track EP just before Halloween. The project features everything from Duff’s hilarious new take on the classic “I Want (a few small things)” and some staring-out-the-window-at-the-snow, melancholic vibes with original song “I Guess It’s Christmas.” Holiday Things comes 24 years after the pop star’s first holiday album, Santa Claus Lane . “Today Santa Claus Lane turns 24, and it has me reminiscing on all the fun we’ve had around the holidays together over the years,” Duff wrote on Instagram. “Let’s do it again this year?” Amen.

Thrice frontman Dustin Kensrue had the same early bird idea as Duff when he released his second holiday album That Spirit of Christmas a week before spooky season had even ended. But don’t expect a hardcore take on Christmas classics. Named after Ray Charles iconic track, the album finds Kensure channeling that same nostalgic holiday spirit across two originals, longtime faves, and a reimagined version of “This Good Night Is Still Everywhere” from his first Christmas album.

This season, even large corporations are spearheading holiday music releases once more. Starbucks has released Holiday Blend , the ubiquitous coffee brand’s first global holiday album in over a decade, which features seven commissioned tracks from Brandi Carlile, Magnus Ferrell, TRÍADA, The Womack Sisters and JYT. What else can get you into the holiday spirit if not hearing Thomas’ groovy take on “Soulful Christmas” while sipping on a peppermint mocha?

Olivia Rodrigo unwrapped her first-ever holiday song this week. No surprise, it’s a New Wave-inspired delight. The pop star even recruited Sex and the City ‘s Cynthia Nixon for a fun music video that fully channels the Christmas spirit. It seems Rodrigo may even have some more holiday cheer in store for us: the vinyl version of “Take Me Home (4 Christmas)” features the unreleased song “Miss This Christmas” on Side B.

entertainment.title: The Rings Of Power: The War Of The Elves And Sauron Explained
entertainment.summary: Expect Season 3 of The Rings of Power to dive right into the fray of the War of the Elves and Sauron in the Second Age. Here's how it goes down in the books.
entertainment.body:
Ben Rothstein/Prime Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Amazon's flagship Middle-earth series, "The Rings of Power," is using Season 3 as a soft reboot. This is partly due to a five-year time jump, one that will launch Middle-earth into the heart of the War of the Elves and Sauron. That multi-year conflict started at the end of Season 2. In the source material, the knock-down, drag-out event leads to one of Sauron's most victorious moments. The Dark Lord gets much closer to total domination of Middle-earth than he ever does in "The Lord of the Rings."

Expect Season 3 to dive right into the fray. By this point in the story, Sauron unleashes his armies across the continent as he starts to swap his deceptive strategy as Annatar for one of a truly Dark Lord bent on conquest, violence, and destruction. We get a brief reference to this war in the source material that the showrunners are primarily working from — the appendices of "The Lord of the Rings." There, in a timeline of Second Age events, it says that the war starts four years before Sauron invades Eriador, kills Celebrimbor, and seizes many of the Rings of Power (events depicted at the end of "The Rings of Power" Season 2 ). After that, we get the single summary line for the next couple of years: "Sauron overruns Eriador."

In the books, this multi-year win streak for the villain starts after nearly a century of preparation (although the show has condensed everything into the span of a few years). But when Sauron finally unleashes his armies, all hell breaks loose — and fast.

Ben Rothstein/Prime In the years that follow the start of the War of the Elves and Sauron, the Dark Lord spreads his influence across the bulk of Middle-earth. Some of this comes through attacks by his Orcish soldiery. But battlefield brute force isn't all. "The Silmarillion" talks about how Sauron uses this time to distribute the Rings of Power that he's captured to Men and Dwarves, too.

As for the Elves, some resist, but most are killed or flee before his growing power. Their only safe havens are the new fortress of Rivendell (which was teased at the end of Season 2) and the High-king Gil-galad's kingdom of Lindon (home of the Grey Havens, where Frodo sails away from Middle-earth at the end of "The Return of the King").

For years, everywhere he goes, Sauron wins. His armies multiply. His power in the East and South, in kingdoms like Harad, Khand, and Rhûn, grows quickly, too. He recruits Men and Orcs into his armies, and for a while, he seems unstoppable. It isn't until the seventh year of the war that the Elves, Men, and Dwarves resisting Sauron get a reprieve. After the Elves ask for aid, the king of Númenor sends a great navy and army. The book "Unfinished Tales" details a series of events where the delayed Númenórean fleet arrives in the nick of time, destroying Sauron's strength before he can defeat the Elves. This is followed by the final battle of the war.

entertainment.title: Janusz Kaminski, the Polish Cameraman Who Taught Hollywood How to See
entertainment.summary: The cinematographer behind 'Schindler's List,' 'Saving Private Ryan' and 'The Diving Bell and the Butterfly' is THR's Visionary of the Year.
entertainment.body:
Like pretty much every great cinematographer, Janusz Kamiński is Polish. As much as any single artist of his generation, he has also taught Hollywood how to see.

But there was a lot of longing in that gray. “Poland is a very lyrical country, to some degree,” he says. “There’s that melancholy, that certain wish for something else.” Theater troupes passed through, and the local cinema promised a world beyond the town. “We were exposed to work that we didn’t experience in real life, but we wanted to experience,” Kamiński says. “The primary reason I left home is because of the theater and movies, and a life of color.”

Kamiński left Poland as a political refugee in 1981, dreaming of American movies. He spoke no English. Landing in Chicago, he spent two years learning the language and then enrolled part-time at Columbia College. In an introductory filmmaking class, he found himself in a group of five. “We had to each pick: One would be the writer, one the actor, one the director, one the producer, and one the cinematographer,” he recalls. “We literally picked straws. I got cinematography. I was 22.”

It was love at first sight. “I found out I really enjoyed creating images. It was just fascinating for me to see the flickering image on 16 mm black and white,” he says. “Just that mystery: Will it be in focus? Will it be properly exposed? Will it have a story?” A professor told him he was good at it and should keep going. “This is not a sad story, but it was the first time anyone every told me I was good at something,” says Kamiński. “In Poland, when I grew up, nobody’s parents said that kind of thing. It was: You have food, you eat, you’re good.”

All his classmates at Columbia wanted to direct, so Kamiński shot their movies. He loaded a station wagon with equipment every weekend and made student films, and picked up commercial work as a camera assistant, an electrician and a grip. One commercial spot a month would pay $250. “My rent was $280, so I was doing good,” he says. “I had a job, and for an immigrant, it’s essential that we support ourselves, because there was no mommy, no daddy, no cousins.”

In the early days, The Hollywood Reporter came to his aid. Back then, in the back of the magazine, THR ran lists of movies going into production, including location shoots. “That’s how I got my first jobs, through The Hollywood Reporter ,” says Kamiński. “I’d look at that films listed and I wouldn’t call on a Tom Cruise movie, but if it was something like Bambis from Hell , I’d call the producer up and say ‘Hi, my name is Janusz Kamiński. I’m a cinematographer. Would you like to look at my work? I got my first two features from that.”

Rist voiced a teenager who was transported to an animated, music video-esque world. In the '90s, audiences could hear Rist all over the place.

New Line Cinema One of Robbie Rist's best-known roles after Cousin Oliver is Michelangelo, the nunchuck-wielding party dude of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles. Rist first voiced Michelangelo in the live-action 1990 movie and returned for "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles II: The Secret of the Ooze" the following year, as well as the third film in '93. He told a "TMNT" fan site that the voice came naturally to him because he grew up in the Valley and he and his childhood friends all talked like stoner surfers. "When the opportunity to do Michelangelo came up I knew him already," Rist explained. "I had went to high school with him."

Rist's extensive voice acting credits include roles in shows like "Batman: The Animated Series," the forgotten sci-fi series "Invasion America," "Totally Spies!," "Lilo & Stitch: The Series," "Jackie Chan Adventures," and the "Powerpuff Girls" reboot. He also voiced Chōji Akimichi, a large and loyal supporting character, in the English dub of the "Naruto" anime and numerous video game adaptations. His big-screen voice credits also include a part in "Balto."

"VO acting is like on-camera acting, only harder," Rist told No Echo , but he still occasionally appears in the flesh, including in a silly role in the so-bad-it's-good TV movie "Sharknado." entertainment.title: Westworld Spawned A Forgotten TV Sequel Series Decades Before HBO's Reboot
entertainment.summary: These violent delights have violent ends, especially for Westworld shows. Between the HBO series and a forgotten '80s sequel, the franchise has bad luck on TV.
entertainment.body:
HBO's "Westworld" was a big deal when it first premiered, but the expensive sci-fi series' legacy started fading once the show was unceremoniously canceled and later removed from HBO Max . Things could have been much worse, though. HBO's series at least ran for four seasons, unlike the "Westworld" TV show from the early '80s that was canceled after three episodes. Premiering on CBS on March 5, 1980, "Beyond Westworld" was a sequel to the 1973 feature film "Westworld."

Written and directed by Michael Crichton, the author behind "The Andromeda Strain" and "Jurassic Park," the original movie took place in a futuristic theme park where humanoid robots allowed guests to experience their fantasy of life in the Wild West until the androids malfunction and actually start killing people. Crichton had no involvement in "Beyond Westworld" other than signing over the rights, and the series ignored the events of the 1976 film sequel, "Futureworld." Instead, it starred Jim McMullan as John Moore, the security chief of the corporation behind Westworld who was tasked with stopping Simon Quaid (James Wainwright), a rogue scientist who wants to use his robots to take over the world. Connie Sellecca, better known for the primetime soap "Hotel," played Moore's assistant.

CBS/YouTube "Beyond Westworld" had the potential to be something of a sci-fi spy series, with John Moore traveling around the world to stop Simon Quaid and his robots' latest evil scheme. It never reached that potential. CBS made five episodes, but canceled the show after airing just three. In Mark Phillips and Frank Garcia's book "Science Fiction Television Series," star Jim McMullan explained that the pilot had a great script and got good reviews. The problems really began when the network started making them rush to write and shoot the subsequent episodes.

"It was like asking someone to deliver a weekly show like 'Mission: Impossible' and not give much time to write these intricate scripts," McMullan said. "They could have been wonderful. We were very disappointed because each time we would get a new script, we were rushing to get it finished. So, we ended up with all this junk and you could feel each show was a little worse than the last one. We tried hard."

McMullan felt that the characters on the show, especially his protagonist, weren't afforded any characterization. Instead, "Beyond Westworld" became an underwhelming chase show — and due to the effects needed to make people look like robots, an expensive one. Ratings fell and so too did the axe. Despite the cancellation, "Beyond Westworld" was nominated for two Emmy Awards: Outstanding Achievement in Makeup and Outstanding Art Direction for a Series. It lost the latter for another now-forgotten series that starred Michael J. Fox .

entertainment.title: Camerimage Opens With a Robot, an AI Reckoning and a Minute of Silence for Kraków
entertainment.summary: The 34th edition of Camerimage kicked off with Luca Guadagnino’s 'Artificial' and included honors for Darren Aronofsky and the THR Visionary Award for cinematographer Janusz Kamiński.
entertainment.body:
The AI elephant in the room took center stage on Saturday at the opening night of the 34th Camerimage Film Festival.

Instead of avoiding the divisive issue of artificial intelligence , the Polish fest, the world’s leading festival for the celebration of the art of cinematography, doubled down.

For the opening address, in place of festival director Marek Żydowicz, Camerimage sent a humanoid robot, called “Edward Warchocki,” on stage. The slightly tottering, Polish-speaking android addressed the crowd before Żydowicz joined it for an extended back-and-forth about the role of AI in cinema. The “hopes and threats” of the technology, Żydowicz stressed , would be a major talking point throughout the seven-day event in Toruń. Related Stories Movies Camerimage Founder Marek Zydowicz on AI, Aronofsky and Why "Cinematographers Are Artists, Not Technicians" Movies PÖFF Stands With Ukraine: A Look at Films Featured at Tallinn Made Despite, and Because of, the War

The theme ran through the three-hour ceremony at the city’s Jordanki Culture Centre, which was regularly interspersed with video messages from Francis Ford Coppola, Gal Gadot, Christopher Nolan, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Steven Spielberg and Ben Affleck, each weighing in on AI in entertainment.

Few filmmakers are as closely associated with the debate as Darren Aronofsky , who was honored with Camerimage’s honorary Award for Director . A vocal advocate of generative AI in filmmaking since launching his AI studio Primordial Soup last year , the Requiem for a Dream and Black Swan helmer said it was his third visit to the festival and that he hoped to keep coming back.

“The reason I come back is because there are very rarely film festivals that celebrate the collaboration of everyone,” he said. “They’re very focused on not just the flashy names and that’s really incredible because it honors everyone who makes films possible for people like me.”

Other honorees included Karolina Gruszka, one of Poland’s most acclaimed film and stage actresses, who received the Marshal of the Kujawy Pomorze Region Film Award. Gruszka, who appeared in David Lynch’s last feature, Inland Empire (which was shot in Poland) paid tribute to the late director as a “master investigator” of stories.

Polish cinematographer Janusz Kamiński, longtime Spielberg collaborator and two-time Oscar winner (for Schindler’s List and Saving Private Ryan ) received The Hollywood Reporter ’s Visionary Award for contributions to cinematography. The festival also paid tribute to the late great Polish director Andrzej Wajda ( Man of Iron , Ashes and Diamonds ), a century after his birth and a decade after his death, with a performance by the Polish Radio Choir – Lusławice giving an a cappella reinterpretation of the music from Wajda’s most important films. Poland’s Senate has declared 2026 “The Year of Wajda.”

After a string of projects, Russell played the iconic Snake Plissken in John Carpenter's "Escape from New York" and its sequel "Escape from L.A."

Russell's filmography boasts varied genre titles including "Big Trouble in Little China," "The Thing," "Backdraft," "Vanilla Sky," "The Hateful Eight," and "Once Upon a Time in... Hollywood." Russell also played Col. Jack O'Neill in Roland Emmerich's "Stargate," which became a beloved television franchise starting with "Stargate SG-1," easily one of the best Syfy shows of all time. Additionally, the actor played Ego the Living Planet in "Guardians of the Galaxy: Vol. 2."

On the television front, Russell belted out an unforgettable performance in "Monarch: Legacy of Monsters." His television credits are as extensive as his film appearances, including shows like "The Fugitive," "Gilligan's Island," the ABC TV movie "Elvis," "What If...?" and "The Madison."

Russell brings a one-of-a-kind star power to the screen while flexing astounding genre versatility, which is why he is today's quote of the day.

entertainment.title: Elon Musk Is Portrayed on ‘SNL’: “The Worst Thing South Africa Has Ever Done”
entertainment.summary: Jeremy Culhane plays the character in the show’s latest attempt to assess its relationship with the mogul.
entertainment.body:
Logo text Elon Musk spent nearly half a billion dollars to get humiliated at the polls, but at least he came away with an SNL parody. Jeremy Culhane played the mogul in an appearance with Weekend Update’s Colin Jost as he tried to make sense of his bruising electoral losses. The actor offered a persuasive impression of the mogul’s halting speeches and nonsensical attempts to change the subject with talk of a future that won’t happen. “Imagine,” Culhane’s Musk ended a sentence several times non-sequiturishly. A few days after his major campaign investments came up fruitless (and in a week when his Cybertruck was officially deemed a failure , compounding the injury), comic Musk sought to change the subject “You’re in the news because you wasted half a billion dollars on the midterms… almost all the candidates you backed lost,” Jost said. Related Stories TV Druski Embodies Elizabeth Holmes in 'You Can See Everything' Spoof on 'SNL' TV James Talarico Crashes 'SNL' Cold Open, Apologizes for Texting Us So Much

“I’m in the news because my car did a flip… it was like a freaking Hot Wheel,” Musk replied with a Buttheadian enthusiasm. Jost pointed out the irony that “you moved to Texas because California was run by Democrats” and now Texas would be too. “How does that make you feel?” Jost asked. “Bad,” Musk said, before cluelessly changing the topic back to a car flip and barrage of so-you-know-uhs the mogul is known for. (In real life, Musk tried to turn the losses into vindication for the conspiracy theories that he was involved in rigging the 2024 election.) The show’s writers piled on when they had Musk ask Grok to treat him to an “epic vulgar-roast” (Culhane’s coinage for what Musk considers a major burn) and the AI chatbot came back with, “You’re the worst thing South Africa has ever done;” “When you’re on TV it feels like a episode of ‘Hate on the Spectrum’;” and “If you have 100 more kids, maybe one of them will talk to you.” Musk has been in the pop-cultural spotlight this fall with Alex Gibney’s four-hour investigative documentary , which deconstructs the myth of mogul and makes a case he is far more dangerous than caricaturist appearances in Hollywood productions may suggest. Musk has recently has been buying up spectrum, spending $1 billion on Skydance and taking flack for allegedly turning off Starshield and potentially endangering Ukrainian lives. The character had recently been played by Mike Myers, as in a cold open appearance a year ago as he maniacally bellowed “Legalize Comedy” behind portrayals of Trump and Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and other appearances in which he did an unhinged air-pounding two-first dance. That impression had a lot of scenery-chewing swings (and more than its share of Mike Myers being Mike Myers), while Culhane Saturday night was more effectively restrained and on-point, leaving the possibility he might be reprising the character on future SNL episodes. Gibney’s film notes how Musk has been savvy at doing cartoonish enough behaviors that people tend to underestimate him, a point that was underscored even in the sketch when, after he went off one more time about a vulgar epic-roast and a car flip, Jost said “I cannot believe you’re the richest person in the world.”

entertainment.body:
Logo text James Austin Johnson was born for this moment — Donald Trump spinning as he is roundly defeated by Democrats — and he rose to meet in Saturday Night Live ’s cold open.

But it was a Democratic politician who stole the show from Trump’s 2026 defeatism tour, as Texas senator-elect James Talarico made a surprise appearance as himself at the end of the sketch.

“I’m James Talarico, the guy who’s been texting you every day asking for five dollars,” the popular Texas politician said as he came out on stage to gasps and cheers from the audience, with Trump mumbly meta-jibing behind him, “In this economy, who can blame you?” Related Stories TV Emma Stone Joins Druski During His 'SNL' Hosting Debut TV After 2026 Midterms, Bill Maher Asks Trump, "Donnie, Are You OK?"

Talarico a moment later invoked the iconic “Live from New York” with Johnson. Talarico drubbed his Republican opponent Ken Paxton by 12 points in the most expensive race in the history of the United States Senate, in part on the back of the grassroots fundraising campaign he was self-mocking on SNL . The result turned a Texas Senate seat blue for the first time in over 30 years.

Before Talarico showed up in Studio 8H, Johnson had been reveling in his presidential character’s anti-moment.

“I didn’t even say it was rigged,” Trump said of the election tallies. “I accepted the results, which is even scarier in a way. It’s like, ‘What the hell is he planning?'” He then said he only cared about his newly redesigned White House ballroom, before allowing under his breath, “Oh my God, I hate my life.”

Talarico’s cold-open surprise cameo echoed moments like Kamala Harris’ 2024 turn-up, in which she played opposite her celebrity impersonator Maya Rudolph ahead of the election, while Hillary Clinton and Sarah Palin also made unexpected appearances as White House candidates more than a decade ago. A senator or senator-elect, however, is rarer, and the moment both reflected and reinforced the emergent media celebrity of the new class of Congressional Democrats, many of them in their 30s or early 40s.

“The next few years are going to be horrible,” he said, pausing a comic beat. “It’s not that they’re Democrats; it’s that they’re Millennials.” He then lamented the return of generational staples like “adorkable” and the show New Girl .

entertainment.body:
Logo text Druski made his Saturday Night Live debut with an assist from his upcoming co-star Emma Stone .

He kicked off his first-ever monologue by acknowledging that his appearance marked the first time an online content creator hosted the show.

“It is a dream to be hosting Saturday Night Live . Apparently, people are saying I’m the first internet content creator, social media influencer, only make you laugh on your phone, TikTok and YouTube and Instagram star to host this show,” he said. “Woo. People say a lot of things about me, honestly.” Related Stories TV 'SNL' Writer Jimmy Fowlie Pays Tribute to Sister Christina Downer After Police Arrest Two for Her Murder TV Druski Signs Deal With Netflix, Sets Church Comedy 'Collect & Praise'

“Some people say I look like a lesbian. I don’t know how true that is,” Druski joked. “Some people say I’m on Ozempic. Could be lies, could be truth to that.”

“But honestly, this is a huge moment for me growing up as a fat kid from the suburbs. Why y’all laughing? My teachers never believed in me, so I just wanna say… Yeah, I’m just lying. “I’m so grateful. When I first started my career, I let them, let me turn my dreams into a full-blown movie convention. Every day I think about how could I possibly repay y’all,” he began, as one of his family members offered, “Some money!”

The comedian recounted the growth his career has seen in recent years, noting, “I am living proof you can bet on yourself and make your dreams come true.” He added, “I just finished filming my first ever movie with Emma Stone, and she is here right now!” The Oscar winner then entered the stage, and the two recounted their time working on The Catch together.

sports.title: Report: Vikings to sign Odell Beckham Jr. to 53-man roster
sports.summary: The move would set Beckham up for his Vikings debut on Monday night.
sports.body:
Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports that the Vikings will sign Beckham to their 53-man roster ahead of the game. Beckham signed to the practice squad in Minnesota a month ago and was elevated to the active roster once without appearing in a game.

Beckham opened the season with the Giants and played in all three of their September games. Beckham saw action on 70 offensive snaps, but was only targeted with one pass and did not make a catch.

The Vikings will not have Jauan Jennings on Monday night due to a calf injury, so there should be a chance for Beckham to be involved in the team’s passing game. That passing game will be led by quarterback Carson Wentz as Kyler Murray will not play due to a hamstring injury.

sports.title: Raiders return to Bay Area — and the jail at Levi's Stadium could be busy
sports.summary: The Raiders left Oakland, for the second time, after the 2019 season.
sports.body:
And, as Matt Barrows of The Athletic notes, the renewal of the rivalry could result in plenty of activity in the 3,500-square-foot holding facility at Levi’s Stadium.

The Raiders played a regular-season game there in 2018. That day, there were 32 arrests . It was the first time the 49ers had hosted a Raiders game since a preseason contest in 2011 that featured multiple incidents of fan violence resulted in a suspension of the annual low-travel-cost exhibition get-together.

Regardless of whether things get interesting in the stands, concourses, parking lots, etc., the game brings plenty of on-field intrigue. Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins and 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan have a relationship that dates back to Cousins’s rookie year with Washington, in 2012. 49ers defensive coordinator Raheem Morris was Atlanta’s head coach during Cousins’s two seasons with the Falcons.

And Raiders coach Klint Kubiak was the 49ers’ passing game coordinator in 2023. Klint’s brother, Klay, has been the 49ers’ offensive coordinator since 2025.

The Raiders are unexpectedly in contention for an AFC playoff berth, at 5-5. The 49ers control the NFC West at 6-1, and they’re in position to force the road to the Super Bowl through Santa Clara.

sports.title: Ja'Marr Chase explodes for 142 receiving yards in first 25 minutes of play in Madrid
sports.summary: The Bengals' star wide receiver is having the best first half of his career.
sports.body:
Chase caught eight passes for 142 yards and a touchdown in the first 25 minutes of play against the Falcons, helping the Bengals take a 21-10 lead over the Falcons.

It’s the most receiving yards that Chase has ever had in the first half of a game in his career.

The rest of the Bengals’ offense hasn’t done anything special, with a total of 91 yards on any play that isn’t a pass to Chase, but they haven’t needed to. Chase is taking over the game.

It’s going to be a long flight home from Spain for the Falcons’ defense if they can’t find a way to stop Chase from running free through their secondary.

sports.title: Cowboys have ideal chance to end streak of allowing 20 or more points
sports.summary: It's been nearly a year since the Cowboys held an opponent under 20 points.
sports.body:
At 1:00 p.m. ET, the Cowboys visit the Colts. And the Colts have scored a total of 17 points since waving the white flag with the same-day trades of guard Quenton Nelson to the Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the 49ers.

Of course, they’ve played a couple of very good defenses, at Minnesota and at Jacksonville. Still, with the organization creating a clear impression that they’ve embarked on a rebuilding plan during the 2026 season — and with trade talk hovering as to running back Jonathan Taylor, quarterback Daniel Jones, and receiver Josh Downs — the Cowboys are catching the Colts at an ideal time for Dallas.

For now, the Cowboys have allowed 20 or more points for 15 straight games. It’s the longest active streak in the league, and the longest streak in franchise history.

The Cowboys last held an opponent under 20 points on November 17, 2025, in a Monday night 33-16 win over the Raiders. Since then, the Cowboys have allowed 21, 28, 44, 34, 34, 23, 34, 28, 20, 34, 30, 24, 23, 21, and 33 points. That works out to an average of 28.7 points allowed per game.

Today’s the day the run could end. If it doesn’t, who knows when it will?

sports.title: Daniel Jones has several million reasons to want to be traded to a contender
sports.summary: A trade would be a financial win-win for Colts and Jones.
sports.body:
Jones’s two-year, $88 million deal has plenty of sweeteners for 2026. And most of them are tied to making it to the playoffs, and winning games once he gets there.

He’s on track to earn up to $550,000 by racking up 90 percent offensive playing time for the season. Through eight games, he has taken 98 percent of the snaps. (Specifically, the term gives him $100,000 for 50 percent, $200,000 for 60 percent, $300,000 for 70 percent, $400,000 for 80 percent, or $550,000 for 90 percent.)

Jones also gets an extra $100,000 for each win in which he plays more than 50 percent of the snaps. To date, he has added $200,000 of a potential $800,000.

If his team wins 10 or more games and he participates in 75 percent of the offensive snaps, Jones gets another $250,000. With 75-percent playing time and a playoff berth, he gets another $250,000. With 75-percent playing time and a division title, he gets another $250,000.

Then comes the package for postseason success, with up to $2.5 million available. With 50-percent playing time and a win in the wild-card round, he gets $500,000. With 50-percent and a win in the divisional round, he gets another $500,000. With 50-percent playing time and a win in the conference championship, he gets another $500,000. With 50-percent playing time and a win in the Super Bowl, he gets another $1 million.

So, yes, Jones has plenty of reasons to want to be moved from a non-contender to a contender.

And the Colts have plenty of reasons to want to get him off the roster. He has a $10.51 million injury guarantee for 2027. At some point, the Colts could be tempted to put him in bubble wrap, like the Giants did to him in 2024.

At that point, Jones would surely repeat his request from two years ago to be released. Because, however, the trade deadline will have passed, he’d be subject to waivers.

sports.title: Bill Belichick, UNC are one win away from bowl eligibility
sports.summary: Former Patriots coach Bill Belichick was back in New England on Saturday, for a game between North Carolina and Connecticut.
sports.body:
The Tar Heels, fueled by three touchdown passes from quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. and 21 points from three Huskies turnovers, ended a two-game losing streak with a 38-21 win .

The victory moved UNC to 5-4 on the season. It puts them one win short of bowl eligibility, with three games to play.

North Carolina finishes its schedule with games against 6-3 Louisville, 4-5 Virginia, and 4-5 NC State.

Now in his second season at the college level, Belichick’s overall record is 9-12.

sports.title: Lamar Jackson's message to teammates: Stay alive, and I'll be back
sports.summary: Jackson is out 6-9 weeks with thumb injury.
sports.body:
Via Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Jackson told teammates this week that he intends to return this season.

Jackson, per Rapoport, is out 6-9 weeks with a fractured and dislocated thumb.

The two-time MVP’s message to the locker room was simple: “Just stay alive, and if you do I will be back.”

The Ravens are currently hanging by a shrinking handful of threads. From 4-1 to 4-5, the Ravens are fading in the AFC playoff picture. But, after losses to the Browns, Bengals, Bills, and Jaguars, the schedule softens moving forward.

First up, they host the currently winless Chargers next Monday night. Then, the Ravens play at Carolina before facing the Texans.

Baltimore, which will debut Jacoby Brissett as the starting quarterback in Week 10, could be 7-5 at the bye.

After that, the stretch run won’t be easy: Bucs, at Steelers, Browns, at Bengals, Steelers. Still, if Lamar could return for the Week 15 game at Pittsburgh, the Ravens could force their way back into one of the seven spots on the AFC playoff tree.

sports.title: Texans are resisting trade interest in players like Jadeveon Clowney
sports.summary: It's the same story every year.
sports.body:
As noted on Sunday morning by Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, the 2-5 Texans have received calls regarding teams that have interest in raiding the roster. The one name mentioned by Garafolo was veteran pass rusher Jadeveon Clowney.

The Texans, however, are waiting to see what happens today. A win over the Chargers in L.A. would move the Texans to 3-5. With a win in hand over the Jaguars and a rematch coming in Week 15, the Texans would still have a chance to catch Jacksonville for the AFC South crown.

A loss to the Chargers would change everything. Beyond falling to 2-6, the Texans will have lost to the lowly Chargers, this year’s official Sixth Sense team that doesn’t yet know it’s dead.

If the Texans lose, the calls will surely intensify — and G.M. Nick Caserio will have some decisions to make.

Clowney surely would welcome the chance to land with a contender. He picked the Texans in large part because he believed they could win the Super Bowl .

sports.title: Mike Vick, Norfolk State lose after his order was ignored
sports.summary: Like a growing number of former NFL players, Mike Vick has become a college football coach.
sports.body:
With 1:34 to play during Saturday’s game between Vick’s Norfolk State and North Carolina Central, Norfolk State led, 28-23. Norfolk State had the ball, facing second and five from the 50. North Carolina Central had no timeouts remaining.

While a pair of knees wouldn’t have fully exhausted the remaining time, Vick told the offense to take a knee in victory formation. Two straight kneel-downs would have resulted in a punt with less than 15 seconds to play.

Instead, Norfolk State lined up in shotgun formation, the quarterback ran to the left, a defender hit him, and the quarterback fumbled.

North Carolina Central recovered at the Norfolk State 37. Five plays later, North Carolina scored a touchdown, on a 26-yard touchdown pass, making the score 29-28. (The two-point conversion attempt failed.)

Twenty-seven seconds remained. Norfolk State drove in position to attempt a game-winning field goal. The 37-yard try missed wide left.

“I don’t know what happened at the end of the game,” Vick told reporters after a loss that dropped Norfolk State to 4-6 on the season. “I put my headset down. I called victory formation. All we had to do was take a knee, kneel the clock out. That’s just situational football. I don’t know what happened in regards to that. I looked up and we was running the ball, and then I seen the fumble. But my final instructions was victory formation. That’s when you kneel it out. And they had, I think, zero timeouts left and the game was over practically.”

“Well, I put my headset down, and I took my headset off because all we had to do was just run it three times, or two times, or kneel it out. That’s called victory. I don’t know what happened. A run play was called. I looked up, I seen us running the ball. I don’t know what happened. I really don’t. I don’t know what the play call was. I don’t know why we even ran that play.

“People will look at that, and that’ll go on as a teaching tape for a lot of teams across the country for years to come. I hate it had to be us. But I called victory formation. Just letting everybody know that. I called victory.”

sports.title: Hall of Fame LB Jack Ham hospitalized after medical emergency at Penn State game
sports.summary: Hall of Fame linebacker Jack Ham, who now serves as a radio analyst for Penn State football, was hospitalized in Seattle on Saturday after experiencing a medical emergency.
sports.body:
Penn State coach Matt Campbell said after the 28-25 win over Washington that Ham was assisted by play-by-play announcer Steve Jones.

“If it’s not for Steve, what he did, I don’t know if we have as good a news as we do right now,” Campbell said, via Adam Rittenberg of ESPN. Campbell added that Jones’s efforts to save Ham were “heroic.”

Ham, 77, has served as the Penn State radio analyst since 2000. He won four Super Bowls, made eight straight Pro Bowls, and was named first-team All-Pro six consecutive times in a 12-year career with the Steelers.

Ham was inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1988, after retiring from football in 1982.

sports.title: Deion Sanders says Colorado deserves better after falling to 3-6
sports.summary: Colorado lost again on Saturday night, and afterward head coach Deion Sanders said he knows his team isn't good enough.
sports.body:
Saturday’s 20-10 loss to Arizona State dropped Colorado to 3-6 this season, and dropped Sanders to 19-27 in four years as Colorado’s head coach.

“The season doesn’t look good,” Sanders said afterward. “It doesn’t look good. I’m not crazy. I can see clearly. You think I’m happy? I’m not happy with the outcomes. I’m not a loser by any means, and I hate the fact that we’re coming up on the short end of these games.”

Sanders said he feels for Colorado fans and players because he doesn’t think he has done enough to put them in a position to win.

“It’s not a personal hurt for me, I hurt because you guys deserve better and the team deserves better. We should win. We should put our best foot forward. And I’m not seeing that,” Sanders said.

Sanders ran through the stats from the game and then said his team hadn’t played well enough.

“The fan base deserves better. They really do,” Sanders said.

“We’ve just got to do better,” Sanders said. “And that starts with me.”

sports.title: Player Personnel Handbook implies that the NFL can delay (or deny) Brandon Aiyuk's reinstatement
sports.summary: The CBA is silent on the issue.
sports.body:
The Brandon Aiyuk case shows that, in the NFL’s view, it definitely is not.

The Collective Bargaining Agreement is silent on the topic of the reserve/left squad list. The relevant language regarding placement (and eventual reinstatement) from the reserve/left squad list appears in the NFL’s Player Personnel Handbook.

In the year when the player is placed on reserve/left squad, he can’t play for his current team or any other team. His season is basically over. The window for reinstatement opens the next year.

Here’s the key language from the Player Personnel Handbook regarding reinstatement: “A player on Reserve/Left Squad must apply to the Commissioner for reinstatement to his club’s Active List. No player on Reserve/Left Squad shall be reinstated in the same season in which he is placed on Reserve. A player applying for reinstatement in a season subsequent to the season in which he is placed on Reserve/Left Squad is prohibited from being reinstated in the last 30 days of the regular season or thereafter during the postseason, and no such player will be reinstated during the period between the trading deadline of a subsequent season and the 30-day deadline unless the club initiates the reinstatement request and the Commissioner approves it.”

While the provision doesn’t say it expressly, the language implies that the Commissioner has apparently unlimited discretion when it comes to approving the application to reinstate the player. In Aiyuk’s case, the Commissioner has dragged his feet since October 27, setting the stage for an apparent effort by the 49ers to leverage Aiyuk’s desire to be reinstated to his willingness to reimburse up to $13 million in previously-paid bonus money.

The NFL Players Association has remained silent throughout the process, and perhaps for good reason. The absence of any provision in the CBA regarding the mechanics of the reserve/left squad list arguably means that the situation falls within the NFL’s “management rights” clause, which allows the various teams “to manage and direct their operations in any manner whatsoever, except as specifically limited by the provisions of this Agreement.”

With no limitations in the CBA as to the operation of the reserve/left squad list (or reinstatement from it), the NFLPA may be without options.

Precedent becomes relevant to the overall analysis. How has the league handled past requests for reinstatement from the reserve/left squad list? If the league has previously not delayed reinstatement (for whatever reason), there’s an argument to be made that it should not be delayed as to Aiyuk.

The Chiefs have lost two straight games after starting the season 5-0. Previewing this matchup, Maurice Elston, a writer at Arrowhead Pride, was kind enough to answer a few questions regarding the 2026 Kansas City Chiefs. - The Chiefs limited their opponents to 10 points or fewer in three of their first five games, but they have allowed a combined 48 points in the last two games. Are the recent struggles on defense just a quality of opponent issue, or are there bigger problems involved? I think there are some bigger issues involved, particularly the Chiefs’ inability to consistently pressure the quarterback and finish possessions on critical downs. Seattle converted 11 of 16 third downs and controlled the ball for nearly 36 minutes. Denver only converted 2 of 11 third downs, so the defense improved in that area, but the Broncos went 2-for-2 on fourth down. The lack of a pass rush ties everything together. The Chiefs failed to record a sack against Seattle and produced only one against Denver. They have only nine sacks through seven games, with one of the NFL’s lowest pressure and sack rates. When you cannot consistently pressure the quarterback, offenses have more time to find favorable matchups. When you combine that with an inability to finish possessions on third or fourth down, it eventually leads to more plays, more yards and more points. According to ESPNFL, the Colts have engaged in trade talks this week regarding Daniel Jones, speaking to “multiple teams.”

The precise language of the report identifies only one team as actually talking to the Colts. From the article, the Ravens “were one team to check in on Jones.” The Ravens ultimately struck a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, whose plunge from No. 1 to No. 3 on the depth chart made it clear to the rest of the league that he was available.

The only other team mentioned by name is the Vikings, and the report points only to "[s]peculation” involving Minnesota. (We’ve been “speculating” about it since the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s loss by the Vikings in Detroit.)

Past ESPNFL reporting on a potential trade for running back Jonathan Taylor ultimately listed five teams as talking to the Colts (Giants, Seahawks, Broncos, Packers, Vikings). The fact that other teams weren’t mentioned as to Jones suggests that, frankly, there may not be other teams.

Really, which current contender would want him? The Vikings are the only potential playoff team that checks the box as possibly needing a starter right now. And only the Vikings and Giants are contenders with which Jones has direct experience. (The Giants wouldn’t want a Jones reunion, and Jones surely wouldn’t want it, either.)

That could change this weekend, obviously. One injury to a starter could alter the dynamics, spurring another contender to pick up the phone and make a push for Jones. The most memorable example of that came 15 years ago, when a broken collarbone to Raiders quarterback Jason Campbell prompted a quick deal for Bengals quarterback Carson Palmer, who had decided he didn’t want to play for the team that had drafted him — and who had yet to report.

Three years ago, Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins popped an Achilles tendon two days before the deadline, forcing the Vikings to scramble at the deadline to do a deal with the Cardinals for quarterback Josh Dobbs.

Absent a multi-week injury to a starting quarterback on a contender that doesn’t believe its backup can hold down the fort, the Vikings may be the only team that wants Jones at the deadline.

sports.title: Myles Garrett: Rams' opponents will have to pick their poison, me or Aaron Donald
sports.summary: Garrett and Donald will play together for the first time on Sunday against the Commanders.
sports.body:
Donald did not play in Week 1 because he was still ramping up for the season after returning from his two-year retirement, and Garret hasn’t played since Week 1 because of knee surgery. Garrett said the two of them together, two multiple-time Defensive Player of the Year award winners side by side, will present a unique challenge for opposing offenses.

“I think offenses really have to pick their poison. Who’s going to be freed up this play? I think either of us are pretty good at winning one-on-one, so we’ll have some fun,” Garrett said. “Going into this season I never thought I’d have the chance, and as you all know he kept us in suspense for quite a while, so it was very exciting, and I’m looking forward to getting on the field and playing some real snaps with him.”

Garrett said his poor performance in Week 1 against the 49ers showed him he needed knee surgery, something he would have preferred to avoid.

“I was frustrated after the game. I knew that wasn’t me, and I was being hampered by something,” Garrett said. “I didn’t want to miss any time, but I had to be realistic about where I was physically, and I had to make the best choice for me and the team.”

But now Garrett is back, and he said he and Donald playing together can give the Rams an “elite defense” for the rest of the season.

sports.title: Rams listed Matthew Stafford with elbow injury because reporters asked about ice on it
sports.summary: On Monday, reporters asked Rams coach Sean McVay about quarterback Matthew Stafford having ice on his throwing arm after Sunday's win over the Chargers.
sports.body:
“Really, it’s because you guys asked me about it earlier in the week,” McVay told reporters on Friday regarding the decision to disclose an elbow injury for Stafford. “It’s more semantical than anything else. It’s normal, like what he told you guys, but because you guys asked me about him having ice on his elbow. . . . He’s been full, hasn’t missed any sort of reps so normal management stuff that he’s been doing over the last few years.”

It conjures memories of the Patriots’ one-time habit of listing former quarterback Tom Brady as “probable” with a “right shoulder” injury. That all started because he had ice on his shoulder in the locker room, reporters inquired, and the team decided to just put him on the injury report every week.

“I haven’t seen any of that,” McVay said. “I told you guys he’d be better equipped to talk about it. He’s been a full participant, been awesome. He’s spinning the ball. He’s been able to activate all parts of the field with great timing, rhythm, and accuracy so he’s been great.”

So either he has an actual elbow injury that the Rams had been concealing, or he doesn’t really have an elbow injury but they listed him as having one because reporters noticed ice on his arm and asked McVay about it. Neither explanation seems to reflect the true spirit of the injury report, which expects real injuries — and only real injuries — to be disclosed.

Either Stafford has an elbow injury that was previously hidden or he doesn’t have an elbow injury and the claim that he has one is a middle finger to the meddling reporters who were doing their jobs. Neither explanation is a preferred alternative to the unvarnished truth.

sports.title: In defending his willingness to spend, Jerry Jones may have admitted to tampering
sports.summary: On Friday, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones tried to reverse the perception/reality that he deliberately underspends on coaches.
sports.body:
“I have been trying to lure very successful coaches away from the teams they were on,” Jones said on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas.

Unless he was referring to college coaches (or high-school coaches), that’s tampering. Period. End of discussion.

It could be false — an effort to bolster the idea that, yes, he’s willing to spend. Still, the effort to put out the frugality fire he started on Tuesday by ridiculously claiming there’s no correlation between coaching pay and winning included a nonchalant concession that he has tried to pry NFL coaches away from their current teams, in blatant violation of the rules.

Will the NFL look into this one? Probably not. Because the league office surely realizes, as the rest of us do, that Jerry was simply saying whatever he had to say to lessen the impact of the accidental truth he told on Tuesday regarding a deliberate reluctance to do whatever he needs to do to make his team as good as it can be.

sports.title: Nick Sirianni admits that he misled reporters about quarterback situation
sports.summary: Instead of covering up one lie with another lie, Sirianni opted to tell the truth that he hadn't.
sports.body:
Because they all do. Particularly in so-called “must-lie” situations.

There’s an art to it. A way to conceal a lie with another lie. On Friday, Eagles coach Nick Sirianni opted not to lie about the fact that he lied on Monday when he told reporters that quarterback Tanner McKee would not be benched.

“ Tanner’s our guy ,” Sirianni said. “We’re not making any changes there.”

On Wednesday, the Eagles made a change there, elevating Joe Milton over McKee. The move was announced after Sirianni had his midweek media availability, which prevented him from being asked questions about the change in position from “Tanner’s our guy” to “Tanner’s not our guy.”

On Friday, Sirianni finally faced the music regarding his comments from Monday. In lieu of coming up with an explanation premised on the idea that what he said was true when he said it and circumstances changed, Sirianni surprisingly admitted that he wasn’t telling the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth to reporters and, in turn, the fans.

“I was going to hold onto that as long as I possibly could, every second, every minute,” Sirianni said. “Again, I’m not real shy with you guys. I’m going to tell you what I want to tell you guys. I respect the job that y’all have to do, but I’m going to tell you what I want to tell you guys because I’m always going to protect the team first and foremost.

“Every second that goes by in a situation like that, that you can hold onto information as long as you possibly can, is a little less time for the opponent to get ready for the game. I know there’s a lot of interest in everything that you all want to hear, the fans want to hear. My job is to win football games, do everything we can do to help win football games, protect the guys here on this football team, and handle everything that I can inside.”

In an industry where the truth is only told when it’s coincidental to strategic interests, it’s jarring that Sirianni told the truth that he was lying. It would have been easy to say, “We took a more careful look at the situation after Monday.” Or, even more simply, “We changed our mind. Shit happens.”
